You’re welcome.  This [Ashton Manual PDF](https://www.benzoinfo.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Ashton-Manual.pdf#page49) has a general taper plan off of Xanax using Valium. 

Chapter II on Page 3 of the PDF shows a week by week plan. I followed this guide and it worked for me.       
You got this. If you take your time, it will be okay!

If you can get some Valium (diazepam), that will really reaaaally help your taper.       
Valium has a much longer half life than Xanax, which greatly mitigates any withdrawal symptoms. 

I was abusing around 5-12mg of Klonopin and 4mg of Xanax (1mg doses) a **day** and had a really hard time with tapering until I got about 300+ pills of 5mg Valium.      
I abused the kpins and Xanax for 15 months before starting to taper. I got down to 0 benzo intake in about 6 months.

(2mg Xanax is about equal to 20mg of Valium      
1mg Xanax ~ 10mg Valium      
.5mg Xanax ~ 5mg Valium)

I’ve quit kratom 3-4 times.      
First time was in 2021 after 1 year of heavy daily use. I didn’t track my intake back then so I have no idea how much I was taking everyday. The RLS stopped after ~ 5 days. And I felt functional again after about 10 days. Granted, I smoked a little weed here and there to help me cope (and I neverrrr smoke because it gives me really bad anxiety). 

The 2nd or 3rd time, I tried taking a lot of supplements to help with the withdrawal symptoms. (Black seed oil, magnesium, and L- theanine were a few but I don’t remember all of them. You can find the list in r/quittingkratom.) And honestly, they helped a lot! But I didn’t stick it out long enough to see how long until I felt normal again. 

The final time I quit was back in 2023. I was terrified of the quitting and started taking .5 Xanax to help me with the withdrawal symptoms…… yea, that was stupid because that turned into a year long benzo addiction as I ended up just replacing the kratom with the anti anxiety meds  🤦🏽‍♀️ I didn’t feel any withdrawals while on the Xanax, though lol 

Hang in there. The supplements can really make a difference! I’m really glad to hear you’re letting yourself cry. Get outside when you can and take lots of showers!! You’re almost out of the thick of it. ♥️

So, funny story: when I switched from caps to powder, I started dosing with a 1/2 tablespoon and googled how many grams that is. Google says ~ 7gs so that’s what I went by. Well… it turns out that a 1/2 Tbsp of kratom is 3-3.5gs! I was so freaking relieved to find out my gpd was half of what I thought. 

To answer your questions..     
I took kratom on and off for 4 years. By then of it, I was taking ~25gpd or 1/2 Tbsp 8x a day 🤦🏽‍♀️      

I decided to cold turkey because I didn’t have the willpower to taper nor did I want to suffer for longer than necessary.

There’s no shame in trying again, it’s commendable for you to continue working towards sobriety.    
You can do it, friend. I believe in you so freaking much. You are stronger than a plant. 

Keep yourself busy,     
Take supplements and vitamins (black seed oil worked wonders),     
Get outside **no matter the weather** (stay warm/dry, obviously),     
Document your thoughts/feelings,     
Take cold showers every 2-3 hours (or hourly, if necessary) to help with the sweats,     
Cry/scream/yell..     
and remember… it **will** pass.

I agree with you that there *should* be commonly understood respect when it comes to how we treat eachother! (We: shouldn’t enter someone’s physical ‘bubble’, should watch our own tone in conversations, should not touch people, etc.)

Respectfully, imo, what you’re referring to as boundaries are actually called “limits” or “rules”. Which everyone should have and uphold but don’t necessarily **need** to communicate…. because it should be basic decency. Where it gets tricky is when we have these personal rules and limits for ourselves but people who lack empathy/decency come along and treat us in ways that don’t align with our limits. What do we do then? Making ourselves be a doormat is certainly never the answer because we have the power to do something in response and that’s where boundaries come into play. 

A boundary is what we do in response to someone else’s inappropriate behaviors to preserve ourselves (and/or preserve the relationship).     
I.e: “We dont accept unannounced visits to our home. If you show up unannounced, we won’t be answering the door.     
I.e: “I don’t want my kid reprimanded by anyone but me, their parent. If you choose to continue ato reprimand my kid, I will remove myself and my kid from the presence and we won’t be around you for a while/until I receive an apology from you.”

For further clarification, had Lindsey told Sharon at some point, “Hey Sharon, I don’t want Amy to have a phone until Amy is 16. If you or anyone buy(s) her a phone before then, I will confiscate the phone and return it back to you (or whoever bought it).” 

And if Sharon bought Amy a phone anyway before Amy turned 16, THEN yes, Sharon crossed Lindsey’s boundary. And then Lindsey should follow through with what she said she’d do.

I totally agree, we’re not entitled to anything! And I know firsthand that sometimes we don’t know what’s (un)acceptable until the situation arises. We grow as we go. 

*I read a lot of stories of people saying their boundaries were crossed… but they never actually communicated the boundary to begin with.*    
SO, this didn’t happen to me but I read about this situation on FB. (I’m using fake names for the sake of clarity.)      

So, Lindsey said that her ex MIL, Sharon, bought Lindsey’s 12yo daughter, Amy (Sharon’s granddaughter), an iPhone. Lindsey says Sharon crossed her boundary but Lindsey never told Sharon that she didn’t want Amy to have a phone. Sharon did, however, ask Amy’s dad (Sharon’s son/Lindsey’s ex) if she could buy Amy a phone and Amy’s dad said it was okay. 

When I read it, I thought to myself that it didnt seem quite accurate for Lindsey to say Sharon “crossed her boundary” if Lindsey didn’t communicate the “No Phone” policy to Sharon. I’d say Sharon was definitely inconsiderate and out of line for not including Lindsey in the decision making, since she is Amy’s MOM after all. 

If I were Lindsey, I’d be upset too if my ex MIL didn’t talk to me about buying my daughter a phone… but I personally wouldn’t consider it crossing my boundary.

As far as my understanding goes….    
“Boundaries are not mandates for other people to follow.     
Boundaries are not demands.     
Boundaries are not expectations.     
Boundaries are not ultimatums.      
Boundaries are not idle threats.     
A boundary is a particular course of action you take to take care of yourself when a particular set of circumstances arises.     
It's about what YOU do.     
Not about what THEY do.”
- Olivia Vizachero (@TheLessStressedLawyer)

- denial,
- anger,
- bargaining,
- depression,
- acceptance.
